title: Rapid evidence handoff, archive, and SIEM integration guide
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic on-call reference for rapidly harvesting, handing off, and archiving forensic evidence for security incidents, and ensuring reliable SIEM ingestion and audit schema alignment. Meant for first responders and SREs on-call during a security event. Focus: RBAC v2 enforcement on exports, automated evidence extraction, SIEM mapping, and a minimal postmortem template.

Scope:
- Incidents that require evidence export (suspicious access, data exfiltration signals, privilege escalation alerts).
- Not a replacement for full IR playbooks; this is the fast lane for evidence collection + SIEM export and handoff.

Quick TL;DR (first 10 minutes)
- Confirm pager: acknowledge incident in PagerDuty and create a short incident thread in #sec-incident (include incident id).
- Capture volatile evidence first: kernel logs, process lists, network connections. Use automated collector where available.
- Lock write/delete permissions for implicated systems via RBAC v2 temporary role block (see command below).
- Trigger automated evidence bundle job: sec-evidence-export --incident $ID --mode fast. If automation fails, follow manual checklist.

Immediate actions (detailed)
1) Acknowledge + triage
   - Acknowledge alert and set incident id: SEC-<YYYYMMDD>-<seq>.
   - Stakeholder ping list: security-oncall, sre-oncall, product-ops if customer-facing.

2) Freeze access (RBAC v2 fast block)
   - Rationale: prevent tampering and reduce blast radius.
   - Command (example):
     # create a temporary deny policy for the affected principal
     rbacctl policies apply --policy-id deny-tmp-$INCIDENT --rules "principal:$USER -> deny:write,delete on resources:vm,storage,logs" --expires "24h"
   - Notes: ensure the deny policy is scoped tightly. Use 'audit-only' for initial tests if unsure.

3) Run automated evidence extraction (preferred)
   - Trigger: sec-evidence-export --incident $ID --mode fast --include logs,kernel,processes,network,kv-cache-manifest --sign-with kms://sec-key-1
   - Where outputs go: evidence-bucket/SEC-<id>/raw/ and indexed metadata to audit-db (audit-events table).
   - If job errors: capture job logs and escalate to infra oncall with job id.

Manual collection checklist (if automation unavailable)
- Host(s): note hostnames + IPs, timestamp (UTC).
- Run and save:
   - sudo journalctl -u inference-runtime -S "-1h" > /tmp/SEC-<id>-journal.log
   - sudo ss -ntp > /tmp/SEC-<id>-sockets.txt
   - ps auxwwf > /tmp/SEC-<id>-ps.txt
   - sudo dd if=/dev/disk/by-path/<impacted> of=/tmp/SEC-<id>-disk-image.img bs=1M count=1024 (only if warranted, coordinate with forensics)
   - model KV cache manifests (path varies by runtime): /var/lib/inference/kvcache/manifests/*.json
- Hash and sign: sha256sum *.log | tee /tmp/SEC-<id>-hashes.txt ; gpg --detach-sign --armor /tmp/SEC-<id>-hashes.txt
- Upload: gsutil cp /tmp/SEC-<id>-* gs://evidence-bucket/SEC-<id>/raw/

SIEM ingestion and audit schema mapping (practical reference)
- Goal: ensure the SIEM gets normalized fields to support triage and long-term hunting. Use these canonical fields when indexing evidence metadata.
- Minimal audit-event schema (keys we push to audit-db and SIEM):
  * event_id: string (SEC-<id>-<seq>)
  * timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
  * host: hostname or instance id
  * actor: principal id (user:email or service:role)
  * actor_roles: [comma-separated roles] (from RBAC v2 at time of event)
  * action: enum (read,write,delete,exec,network-connect,privilege-escalation,evidence-export)
  * resource: resource id (vm,storage,path,kvcache-id)
  * outcome: success|failure|unknown
  * evidence_uri: gs://... or s3://... (signed, short-lived link)
  * checksum: sha256 hex
  * chain_of_custody: user-timestamp-role (see below)
  * tags: list (e.g., "suspicious-login", "high-risk-principal")

- SIEM field mapping example (ELK/left as pseudo mapping)
  audit.event_id => ecs.event.id
  audit.timestamp => @timestamp
  audit.host => host.name / host.id
  audit.actor => user.name / user.id
  audit.actor_roles => user.roles
  audit.action => event.action
  audit.resource => file.path / cloud.instance.id
  audit.outcome => event.outcome
  audit.evidence_uri => url.original
  audit.checksum => file.hash.sha256
  audit.chain_of_custody => event.reference_chain

Retention and archival
- Evidence retention default: 1 year in cold archive (GCS Nearline/Glacier equivalent), 90 days in hot evidence-bucket.
- Chain of custody: append one line per handoff: "<timestamp> | <actor> | <action> | <notes>". Store this alongside evidence metadata as a plain text ledger.

RBAC v2 considerations for evidence access and exports
- Principle of least privilege: only roles tagged 'forensics' + incident-owner can retrieve raw evidence bundles.
- Audit-only mode: before broad enforcement, use RBAC v2 'audit-only' to validate deny rules won't block ops.
- Emergency bypass: define a short-lived emergency token flow (requires dual-approval).
- Example access policy id schema: sec:evidence:access:incident:<id>:role:forensics

Automation knobs (dev/infra notes)
- sec-evidence-export service features:
  * modes: fast (volatile prioritized), full (includes disk images, model artifacts)
  * sign-with: KMS key uri (automatically records signing metadata in audit-db)
  * retention-label: hot|cold
- Reliable upload strategy: multipart + checksum validation + retry (backoff). Record each attempt to audit-db with attempt_id.
- SIEM ingest service should validate schema and reject badly-formed messages (send to dead-letter queue). Monitor dlq size > 0 as alert.

Postmortem / short incident writeup template (fill during or immediately after incident)
- Title: short descriptive (e.g., "SEC-2025-02-07-priv-escalation-redis")
- Incident id: 
- Timeline (UTC): bullet timestamps with actor and short action (try to keep to 1-line per step)
- Root cause hypothesis: short
- Evidence exported: uri list (gs://...) and checksum list
- RBAC changes applied: policy ids applied and why
- Mitigations (temporary): list
- Permanent fixes / follow ups: assign owners + due dates (JIRA tasks)
- Lessons learned / detection gaps
- Final classification (severity, customer impact)

Chain of custody example (plain text ledger)
2025-02-07T02:12:34Z | a.patel@redwood.ai | evidence-export | created raw bundle (sign:kms://sec-key-1)
2025-02-07T02:35:12Z | infra-oncall | verified checksum and moved to cold-archive

Common troubleshooting and FAQs
- Q: Export job stuck in queued state?
  A: check pubsub backlog and export-worker logs. Restart worker: systemctl restart sec-evidence-export-worker. If persistent, escalate to infra team and run export with --mode manual --no-daemon.
- Q: SIEM shows null actor_roles?
  A: likely RBAC v2 sync lag. Re-run rbacctl sync --target audit-db and reindex the last 30 minutes.
- Q: Need to give exec access to contractor for short window?
  A: Create time-bound role using RBAC v2 CLI and require security approval in the incident channel.

Notes to self (raw brainstorm snippets, unresolved)
- Could we auto-truncate model KV cache manifests to reduce sensitive content exposure? (pros/cons)
- Verify that export signing key rotation is documented and test restore from archived secret state.
- Should build an "evidence review" Slack workflow for legal + security to sign off before customer notification.
- TODO: Add sample Kibana dashboard query for incidents by actor_roles and action over 30d.

Appendix: quick commands and references
- List active RBAC deny policies: rbacctl policies list --filter "deny-tmp"
- Revoke a temp policy: rbacctl policies revoke deny-tmp-$INCIDENT
- Start a fast evidence export (example): sec-evidence-export --incident SEC-20250207-01 --mode fast --include logs,kernel --sign-with kms://sec-key-1 --notify-channel #sec-incident
- Upload verify: gsutil ls -L gs://evidence-bucket/SEC-20250207-01/ | grep "Hash (sha256):"

End (this doc is intentionally pragmatic and choppy — it is an on-call cheat sheet more than a formal SOP).

Unresolved/Followups (assign before close):
